findings.description: The loop at line 1112 iterates j <= keys_result->numkeys, but slot_buffer is allocated for numkeys ints (line 1110) and keys_result->keys has only numkeys valid entries (0..numkeys-1). The final iteration reads keys[numkeys].pos -- a zero-filled keysbuf entry (pos 0, hashing argv[0]) for <=6 keys and a heap out-of-bounds read for >6 keys -- and writes slot_buffer[numkeys] past the heap allocation at line 1115. The base version used j < numkeys; the fix is to restore j < numkeys (the dead slot_buffer can be removed entirely).
findings.failureMode: Any keyed command in cluster mode triggers a heap buffer overflow and out-of-bounds read, causing memory corruption or a crash, and single-key commands are spuriously reported as CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT when the command name hashes to a different slot.
findings.title: Off-by-one loop in extractSlotFromKeysResult reads and writes out of bounds

findings.description: The new code calls malloc at line 1110 and free at lines 1120 and 1124, violating the repository mandate to use the zmalloc/zfree wrappers; src/server.h marks malloc/free deprecated for exactly this reason. Running make -C src cluster.o with REDIS_CFLAGS="-Werror" fails with three deprecated-declaration errors at these lines, and the allocation bypasses Redis memory accounting with an unchecked return value. Replace malloc/free with zmalloc/zfree, or remove the unused slot_buffer allocation.
findings.failureMode: The mandated -Werror build fails to compile, and at runtime the allocation is untracked by Redis memory accounting and dereferenced without a NULL check on allocation failure.
findings.title: Direct malloc/free instead of zmalloc/zfree in extractSlotFromKeysResult

findings.description: The rename of pageActionStack to trailingPageActionStack is applied at every other site, but this line substitutes a second browserActionStack, so trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews are never included in stacks. updateActionStack sets alpha=0 on newly added buttons and updateToolbarLayout is the only place restoring alpha=1, so new trailing buttons stay at alpha 0. The base line read pageActionStack.arrangedSubviews, confirming trailingPageActionStack is the intended operand.
findings.failureMode: Newly appearing trailing page-action buttons such as reload or reader mode remain invisible and untappable after toolbar configuration.
findings.title: Trailing page actions omitted from alpha restore

findings.description: This line changed toolbar.leadingAnchor from leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor (base) to rightSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor, while the next line pins toolbar.trailingAnchor to rightSkeletonAddressBar.leadingAnchor. setupSkeletonAddressBarsLayout pins the right skeleton's leading to the container trailing with width near the container width, so its trailing lies far beyond its leading and the two toolbar constraints are inverted and unsatisfiable. This path runs whenever toolbarHelper.isSwipingTabsEnabled is true on iPhone.
findings.failureMode: With swiping tabs enabled, Auto Layout cannot satisfy the address toolbar constraints and the toolbar is collapsed or mispositioned instead of spanning the container.
findings.title: Toolbar leading anchor pinned to wrong skeleton bar

findings.description: The base computed hasPageActions from pageActionStack, which this diff renames to trailingPageActionStack everywhere else, but this line now reads leadingPageActionStack. The divider view sits between locationView and trailingPageActionStack (its trailing anchor equals trailingPageActionStack.leadingAnchor), so its width must follow the trailing stack. AddressBarStateTests show common states with trailing actions and zero leading actions, where the divider width now incorrectly becomes 0 instead of the configured 4.0, and leading-only states get a phantom divider.
findings.failureMode: The address-bar divider disappears when only trailing page actions are present and appears spuriously when only leading actions are present, producing wrong spacing next to the URL field.
findings.title: Divider width keyed to leading instead of trailing actions

findings.description: isLandscape is assigned here and never read anywhere in setupSkeletonAddressBarsLayout or the file, so the stated landscape adjustment never happens. A swiftc check confirms an unused immutable value emits a compiler warning, and UIApplication.statusBarOrientation is API_DEPRECATED since iOS 13 in the SDK header while the repository already provides UIWindow.isLandscape via the window scene in UIWindow+Extension.swift. Removing the dead declaration is the fix unless the value is actually consumed.
findings.failureMode: Every build of this file gains unused-variable and deprecated-API warnings from dead code that performs no layout adjustment.
findings.title: Unused landscape check uses deprecated API

findings.description: The diff deletes DownloadToast's nested UX struct (which held buttonSize = 40) and replaces both UX.buttonSize constraints with raw 40 literals at lines 192-193. AGENTS.md rule 13 mandates UI constants be defined in a nested UX struct, and a Swift 6 typecheck replica of a UIView subclass with a nested UX struct compiles cleanly, so the Swift 6 migration did not require removing it. Restoring the UX struct and referencing UX.buttonSize fixes both sites.
findings.failureMode: The close-button size becomes scattered magic numbers that violate the mandated UX-struct organization and can desynchronize if only one literal is edited later.
findings.title: DownloadToast inlines button-size magic numbers after deleting its UX struct

findings.description: The new controller guards createInvite with @Roles("TEAM_MEMBER"). RolesGuard uses hasMinimumRole over TEAM_ROLES [TEAM_OWNER, TEAM_ADMIN, TEAM_MEMBER], so a plain MEMBER satisfies the TEAM_MEMBER minimum and is allowed through. The parallel organizations-teams-invite controller requires TEAM_ADMIN, the tRPC createInvite handler requires OWNER/ADMIN fallback roles, and the added e2e spec expects a MEMBER to receive 403; the fix is @Roles("TEAM_ADMIN").
findings.failureMode: Any non-admin team member can mint a 7-day invite link and admit arbitrary outsiders to the team, bypassing the admin-only authorization.
findings.title: Invite endpoint allows TEAM_MEMBER instead of TEAM_ADMIN

findings.description: The new-token branch stores the random hex in verificationToken.token with identifier `invite-link-for-teamId-${teamId}`, but returns newToken.identifier while buildInviteLink is called with the real token. The base code returned the token variable and the existing-token branch in the same method returns existingToken.token, confirming the defect; the fix is to return newToken.token. The returned value is therefore the constant per-team identifier, so inviteLink does not contain it and a later lookup by that token finds no VerificationToken.
findings.failureMode: Every newly created invite returns an unusable constant token that never matches the stored verification token, breaking token consumers and the unique-token-per-request contract.
findings.title: createInvite returns identifier instead of generated token

findings.description: The base code returned the /teams teamInviteLink when !isOrgContext and fell through to the /signup orgInviteLink for organization context; the diff changes the guard to if (isOrgContext). The variable names teamInviteLink/orgInviteLink and the organization invite output example (a /signup URL) confirm the base mapping; the fix is to restore if (!isOrgContext). As written, organization and regular-team invites each receive the other context's URL.
findings.failureMode: All invite links point to the wrong flow: org invitees get /teams instead of signup/getting-started and regular-team invitees get signup instead of /teams, also regressing existing tRPC and org API callers.
findings.title: buildInviteLink organization condition inverted

Head wraps the call in an unstructured Task that strongly captures the checked service, while onDismiss/onComplete (lines 290-296, 318-322) can nil the service and finish launch before the Task runs. The stale service then still executes, because OnboardingService is @MainActor and the closure type is already @MainActor (OnboardingFlowViewModel.swift:12), the fix is to remove the Task wrapper and call handleAction directly.
findings.failureMode: An onboarding action runs after dismissal, presenting sync/settings or firing completion twice so didFinishLaunch/startBrowser executes twice.
findings.title: Unstructured Task defers onboarding action past dismissal

findings.description: Line 309 changes write_and_make_executable to return Result<(), FileWriteError>, and prepare_tools (returning crate::Result) propagates it with `?` at lines 232, 239, 245, 251 and 259, but crates/tauri-bundler/src/error.rs has no From<FileWriteError> for crate::Error (only From<io::Error> and other listed types). The manual Display/Error impls at lines 291-307 also violate AGENTS.md rule 8 requiring thiserror for custom error enums, and the added chain makes line 312 fail rustfmt. findings.description: Line 243 changed the base `if !gtk.exists()` guard to `if gtk.exists()`, while the parallel gstreamer block at line 249 correctly keeps `!gstreamer.exists()`. On a fresh tools cache the inlined linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh is therefore never written, so the unconditional `--plugin gtk` linuxdeploy invocation cannot find it. Fix by restoring `if !gtk.exists()`.
findings.failureMode: First-time AppImage bundling fails because linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh is missing from the tools directory.
findings.title: Inverted gtk exists check skips plugin on fresh cache

findings.description: The base write_and_make_executable wrote the file first and then set mode 0o770; lines 312-313 swap the order to call fs::set_permissions before fs::write. All callers invoke it only when the destination does not yet exist (for example lines 228, 237 and 249), so set_permissions fails with NotFound and the data is never written. Fix by writing the file before setting permissions.
findings.failureMode: On a fresh cache every prepare_tools download/inline write fails with a permissions NotFound error, aborting AppImage bundling.
findings.title: set_permissions called before file is written

findings.description: Line 235 maps `i686` to `linuxdeploy_arch` and line 236 uses it for the local filename, but line 238 changed the download URL from `linuxdeploy-{linuxdeploy_arch}.AppImage` in the base to `linuxdeploy-{arch}.AppImage`. For arch `i686` the URL no longer matches the mapped artifact name the code intends to fetch. Fix by using `{linuxdeploy_arch}` in the download URL.
findings.failureMode: Bundling for i686 fails with a failed or wrong linuxdeploy download (404) on a fresh cache.
findings.title: linuxdeploy URL uses arch instead of linuxdeploy_arch

findings.description: The loop uses j <= keys_result->numkeys where the base used j < numkeys, so the final iteration reads keys_result->keys[numkeys].pos and writes slot_buffer[numkeys] into an allocation of only numkeys ints. For a single-key command the zero-initialized keysbuf gives pos 0, hashing argv[0] (the command name) as a phantom key and usually returning a false CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT; for more than MAX_KEYS_BUFFER keys, getKeysPrepareResult allocates keys at exactly numkeys entries, so the read is a heap out-of-bounds read whose garbage pos is dereferenced via argv[pos]. The slot_buffer write is a heap out-of-bounds write on every same-slot command that reaches it.
findings.failureMode: Cluster-mode keyed commands are falsely rejected as cross-slot, corrupt the heap, or crash the server; change the loop bound to j < keys_result->numkeys.
findings.title: Off-by-one in extractSlotFromKeysResult reads and writes past buffers

findings.description: The new code calls malloc at line 1110 and free at lines 1120 and 1124, violating AGENTS.md rule 2 requiring zmalloc/zfree, and src/server.h marks malloc/free deprecated. Running make -C src cluster.o with REDIS_CFLAGS="-Werror" fails with three deprecated-declaration errors at exactly those lines, while the other changed objects compile cleanly. The allocation also bypasses zmalloc used-memory accounting and its return value is never checked before slot_buffer[j] is written.
findings.failureMode: The mandated -Werror build fails on cluster.o; remove the dead slot_buffer allocation or replace malloc/free with zmalloc/zfree.
findings.title: Direct malloc/free violates zmalloc mandate and fails the -Werror build

findings.description: The guard at line 38 (`if rendered is not None and not isinstance(rendered, str)`) exempts None, so `return rendered` at line 40 returns None despite the declared `-> str` return type. Full basedpyright (`make type-check`) fails with exactly this error: template_renderer.py:40:16 "Type str | None is not assignable to return type str". A probe with an executor returning {"result": None} or {} confirms render_template returns None, after which TemplateTransformNode._run crashes on len(rendered) instead of returning a FAILED NodeRunResult; the fix is to raise TemplateRenderError whenever the result is not a str, including None.
findings.failureMode: A code executor response with a missing or None "result" makes the node raise TypeError from len(None) instead of a handled FAILED result, and the basedpyright type-check gate fails on this line.
findings.title: Renderer returns None for missing/None result instead of raising TemplateRenderError

findings.description: @Roles("TEAM_MEMBER") sets the minimum role, and RolesGuard's hasMinimumRole over TEAM_ROLES=[OWNER, ADMIN, MEMBER] therefore admits a plain MEMBER. The parallel organizations teams invite controller uses @Roles("TEAM_ADMIN"), the tRPC createInvite handler restricts invites to OWNER/ADMIN fallback roles, and the new e2e spec itself expects a MEMBER to receive 403. The decorator should be @Roles("TEAM_ADMIN").
findings.failureMode: Any regular team member can mint a shareable invite link that lets arbitrary people join the team, bypassing the admin-only restriction.
findings.title: Invite endpoint requires only TEAM_MEMBER instead of TEAM_ADMIN

findings.description: This is the only file under apps/api/v2/src importing @calcom/features, which apps/api/v2/package.json does not declare as a dependency and which ships raw TypeScript (main: index.ts, no build output); a workspace-symlink require.resolve simulation of the extensionless subpath fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND. The parallel organizations invite controller imports the same class from @calcom/platform-libraries, which re-exports TeamService (packages/platform/libraries/index.ts) and builds to dist/index.cjs for the plain-node production runtime. findings.failureMode: The production API v2 process (node dist/apps/api/v2/src/main.js) crashes at startup with Cannot find module '@calcom/features/ee/teams/services/teamService'.
findings.title: TeamService imported from unbuilt @calcom/features instead of @calcom/platform-libraries

findings.description: The return uses newToken.identifier, which is the constant string `invite-link-for-teamId-${teamId}` set at creation, while inviteLink is built from the random token; the base code returned token and the existing-token branch returns existingToken.token. Consequently the returned token is identical on every request for a team and is not contained in inviteLink, contradicting the new e2e assertions. It should return token (newToken.token).
findings.failureMode: Clients receive a predictable non-secret identifier as the invite token that cannot be redeemed to join the team, and successive invites appear to share one token.
findings.title: createInvite returns the token identifier instead of the generated token

findings.description: The diff changes `if (!isOrgContext)` to `if (isOrgContext)` for returning the /teams link, swapping both branches relative to the base code. Per the base behavior and the PR description, organization-context invites must use /signup with the getting-started callback and regular-team invites must use /teams; this shared helper also serves the tRPC createInvite handler and the organizations invite endpoint. The negation should be restored.
findings.failureMode: Organization and sub-team invitees are sent to /teams while regular-team invitees are sent to the /signup getting-started flow, so every invite link routes to the wrong join path.
findings.title: buildInviteLink organization condition is inverted

findings.description: This field always binds the status select to trigger.expect, while FlowRunStateTriggerFields (lines 21-25) and the new DeploymentStatusTriggerFields (line 31) bind Proactive ("Stays in") selections to trigger.after and Reactive selections to trigger.expect. Selecting Stays in + Paused therefore submits expect=["prefect.work-pool.paused"], a proactive absence-of-paused trigger, instead of after=["prefect.work-pool.paused"]. findings.description:
String.split always returns at least one element, verified with node: "".split("
") is [""] and "a
".split("
") is ["a", ""], so the lines.length > 0 check can never select undefined and blank or trailing lines are stored as empty event names. findings.description: The diff changes strict from true at the base revision (verified via git show of ui-v2/tsconfig.app.json) to false, weakening the tsc -b --noEmit validation run by the validate:types script in ui-v2/package.json. findings.description: validateCreateScheduleInput only checks that input is an object with a non-empty name, then returns the whole object cast as CreateScheduleInput without validating schedule or eventTypeId. findings.description: Both validation failures throw plain Error objects, violating the repository rule that custom errors extend a base type with a typed code (packages/lib/errors ErrorWithCode with ErrorCode, or HttpError with a status code). findings.description: The deleted line built the pattern as keyword[:30].encode('unicode_escape').decode('utf-8') with \u doubled, matching the \uXXXX sequences produced by json.dumps (default ensure_ascii=True) stored in the LongText WorkflowRun.inputs/outputs columns (e.g. tasks/workflow_execution_tasks.py json.dumps). The replacement applies only escape_like_pattern to the raw keyword, so a non-ASCII keyword is searched literally against text that stores it as \uXXXX. Fix by restoring the unicode_escape conversion (and escaping LIKE wildcards in the converted value without breaking the \u sequences).
findings.failureMode: Keyword search over workflow app logs returns no results for non-ASCII (e.g. Chinese) terms present in run inputs/outputs.
findings.title: Workflow log keyword search drops unicode_escape handling for JSON inputs/outputs

findings.description: escape_like_pattern escapes %, _ and \ with a backslash (e.g. '50%' -> '50\%', 'test_data' -> 'test\_data'), but this query declares ESCAPE '|' on a parameterized pattern. With '|' as the escape character, \% is a literal backslash followed by a % wildcard and \_ requires a literal backslash in the text, verified against a reference LIKE engine where the '|'-escape pattern matched only the backslash-containing row. Fix by using ESCAPE '\' (single backslash) to match escape_like_pattern.
findings.failureMode: IRIS fallback full-text search for any query containing %, _ or \ returns wrong/empty results instead of literal matches.
findings.title: IRIS LIKE escape character '|' does not match backslash escaping

findings.description: The 'contains', 'start with' and 'end with' branches pass escape="\\" to like(), but 'not contains' calls json_field.notlike(f"%{escaped_value}%") with no escape argument. Without an explicit ESCAPE, backends with no default backslash escape treat \% and \_ as a literal backslash plus wildcard, so the escaped value does not match literally. Fix by passing escape="\\" to notlike() like the sibling branches.
findings.failureMode: A 'not contains' metadata filter for a value containing % or _ (e.g. '50%') fails to exclude matching documents and returns wrong retrieval results.
findings.title: 'not contains' metadata filter escapes value but omits ESCAPE clause

findings.failureMode: The changed line violates the mandatory snake_case naming rule for Python variables.

findings.description: The BUILD002 error gained the condition '$(AspNetCorePatchVersion)' == '1', so it only fires during the 10.0.1 cycle. docs/BuildErrors.md states this non-suppressible error applies to servicing builds generally because they should not change package references. When the patch version increments to 2, a project can drop a BaselinePackageReference and the build will succeed instead of raising BUILD002. Remove the patch-version clause so the guard covers every servicing patch.
findings.failureMode: From 10.0.2 onward, a breaking package-reference removal in a servicing update builds and ships undetected instead of failing with BUILD002.
findings.title: BUILD002 servicing guard disabled for patch versions above 1

findings.description: rewriteClientCommandVector is called with argc=6 but seven robj arguments (HSETEX, key, KEEPTTL, FIELDS, 1, field, newobj). rewriteClientCommandVector in src/networking.c copies only argc varargs, so the final value newobj is silently dropped and the propagated command is 'HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field'. hsetexParseArgs rejects that with an arity error, and the added test expects '{hsetex h1 KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 f1 *}' including the value. Fix by passing argc 7.
findings.failureMode: Every HINCRBYFLOAT increment is rejected on replicas and lost on AOF replay, so replica and restarted data diverge from the master.
findings.title: Wrong argc truncates replicated HSETEX value

findings.description: The base passed HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE | HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL to hashTypeSet, but the changed line drops HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL. Without that flag hashTypeSet explicitly clears any existing field expiry (listpack-ex and hashtable paths), unlike hincrbyCommand at line 2506 which still keeps it. After 'HSETEX h1 EX 100 FIELDS 1 f1 1' then 'HINCRBYFLOAT h1 f1 1.1', the master reports HTTL -1 while a replica applying HSETEX KEEPTTL would keep the TTL. Fix by restoring HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL.
findings.failureMode: Hash fields lose their expiration on the master on every HINCRBYFLOAT and never expire, diverging from the replica TTL this PR intends to preserve.
findings.title: HINCRBYFLOAT now clears field TTL on master
